scope: Theorem 6.1 (The metric family) of the manuscript “Purely cosmetic surgery on knots in the three-sphere” (preprints/Purely-Cosmetic-Surgery-on-Knots-in-the-Three-Sphere-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 306 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ee916c92b825a868), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 68-69. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. statement: For the fixed finite stack, there are families with the following properties. They are defined for all sufficiently small ϵ > 0, all sufficiently small regularizers d > 0, and arbitrarily long finite auxiliary rational collars. The auxiliary bounds may depend on ϵ and the fixed problem. The family parameter is the original cube of interval parameters, with no added boundary faces. (i) At its genuine faces the family has independent product length collars at Ji and ∂Ni, compatible at intersections of faces. The Ji cross-sections are round. On a component separated by Ji, 68 the limiting data depend only on the interval parameters retained on that component. The Ni metric is complete with positive scalar curvature and a positive-scalar-curvature product end. Its link and its scale on the stretching collar are independent of the tangential cube parameters. The link is joined to the round lens metric through positive-scalar-curvature metrics. These metric choices are common to the two bit terms compared at that lens face. (ii) On the positive-width toric region of a macro constructed below, as d → 0 the retained main piece has a complete metric conformal to a toric Kähler metric with positive cohomology ray represented by H = U + aX1 + b0X2, 0 ≤ a, b0 ≤ 1 4, a + b0 > 0. (6.3) It has nonnegative scalar curvature, with strict positivity on an open set. A zero coefficient removes the corresponding outer part by a C1,i separation; a coefficient 1/4 separates Ni. The class H is supported rationally on the retained main piece in all these cases. Its positive rank is one. (iii) Every macro in the small-width replacement region contains an S2 × S1 × I tube, with fiber U, of length comparable to ϵ−1. On its bulk the metric is, or approaches smoothly, glong = gS2(1/ √ 2) + 1 2 dξ2 + 2 dθ2 x. (6.4) The same description holds for every toric macro whose normalized length L = 1/(a + b0) tends to infinity. All such tube lengths are O(ϵ−1). The tubes lie in C0 and are disjoint from both middle spheres Ji. (iv) Along any sequence of these parameters, every additional unbounded region is one of the following: an exact rational product collar, an annulus approaching a positive-scalar-curvature product, or one of the tubes in (iii). The remaining pieces, after the specified satellite rescalings, have uniformly bounded geometry on fixed truncations. There are only finitely many such pieces for the fixed stack. Away from fixed-length tube ends, the error from (6.4), with any fixed number of spatial derivatives, tends to zero as the distance from both ends tends to infinity. In particular the integrated errors used in Section 7 are o(ϵ−1), uniformly under deeper regularization and longer auxiliary rational collars. For scalar-curvature costs, the middles of the Yj collars are omitted, retaining prefixes of length O(ϵ−1/2); no positivity is required on a Yj cross-section. (v) For each fixed real cohomology class Λ there are closed comparison forms with its prescribed vertical flux on these tubes, zero curvature on the long parts of rational collars, and o(ϵ−1) energy away from the tubes. More precisely, the uniform comparison and error assertions are those of Lemma 6.10. The construction is smooth at finite parameter values and has the ordinary product description on every genuine length collar. Only spatial derivative estimates are asserted uniformly as lengths diverge; no bound on derivatives in a compactifying length coordinate is needed.
